title: [SEP2-7] Undelayed removal rotations let an IO see that a member was removed and which subscriber w
description: Review finding SEP2-7: Undelayed removal rotations let an IO see that a member was removed and which subscriber was dropped (lens SEP2). Location: spec/10-relays.md:564, :837; spec/05-messaging.md:256; ARCHITECTURE.md:392-397; spec/12-security.md:26. Fix: The premise that "periodic rotations [are] batched, delayed" is wrong. 10:837 requires delay only for "new channels and DM groups", so periodic and removal rotations are not timing-distinguished by the spec. The real signal is the subscriber that stays on the old token (10:564 "the same subscribers move across"). That gives the IO pseudonymous removal events, which neither §9 nor 12.3 states. Fix: add the disclosure sentence to ARCHITECTURE §9 and spec §12.3/§12.4 ("An IO can see which subscribers do not move to a rotated key's token, and so can infer that a removal occurred and which connection or push handle it affected"). Drop the optional timing recommendation, since it addresses a difference the spec does not create. Full text: notes/review2/SEP2-verified.md and notes/review2/SEP2.md.
